items.title: Mark van Bommel kon zelf zijn ogen niet geloven: "Dat ze het zo goed kunnen, had ik niet verwacht"
items.summary: Mark van Bommel zag zijn Rode Duivels met 4-1 winnen van Italië en was achteraf uiteraard bijzonder tevreden. De bondscoach had gehoopt dat zijn spelers snel zijn ideeën zouden oppikken, maar de manier waarop ze zijn voetbalvisie nu al uitvoeren, heeft ook hem verrast. Vooral de snelheid waarmee de groep zich heeft aangepast, stemt hem tevreden.

items.title: Van Bommel genoot van Belgische masterclass: 'Dit had ik niet verwacht'
items.summary: Mark van Bommel heeft zondagavond zijn eerste grote hoogtepunt als bondscoach van België bereikt. De Rode Duivels zetten Italië met speels gemak aan de kant (4-1) en hebben daarmee een ticket voor de kwartfinale van de Nations League veiliggesteld. Van Bommel genoot langs de zijlijn en verklaarde na afloop waarom hij Romelu Lukaku geen speeltijd gaf.

items.summary: Thomas Tuchel kan terugkijken op een enerverende avond. Met een zege in Madrid maakte de bondscoach van Engeland een einde aan de imposante reeks van Spanje. Tuchel zag zijn elftal nog niet eerder zo goed spelen.

items.title: England fend off fiery Spain fightback after Anderson’s red to top Nations League group
items.summary: It was the game to show Thomas Tuchel where his rebooted England team had got to; surely the ultimate test in international football. Spain in Spain. A world champion team who, in Tuchel’s words, had “forgotten how to lose.” Before this Nations League group decider, they had been beaten only once in 43 matches – on penalties against Portugal in the final of this competition last year. What England produced for 65 minutes was extraordinary. What followed was equally so for different reasons. When it was over, England had made the most sensational of statements. Back in 2018, on their previous visit to Spain, England won 3-2 in Seville in the Nations League; it was one of Sir Gareth Southgate’s most famous results, an ignition point. It was the same scoreline and the same feeling for Tuchel on Sunday night. Continue reading...

items.title: Ronaldinho makes debut for Italian side Ravenna after 11-year hiatus in playing career
items.summary: Brazil legend plays first half for Serie C club at age 46 ‘Is this my last one? I don’t know,’ Ronaldinho says Ronaldinho played 45 minutes on his return to professional football in Italy. The 46-year-old Brazil great announced in June that he had signed for the Serie C side Ravenna, 11 years after he appeared to have brought his illustrious career to a close with Fluminense. Five months later, he was in the starting lineup as Ravenna faced their local rivals Forlì. Ronaldinho, wearing the No 10 shirt, entered the stadium to great fanfare, with the 5,000-capacity Stadio Bruno Benelli adding a temporary 1,800-capacity stand – dubbed “R10” – for the occasion. Flares and smoke bombs were let off in the stands while Andrea Bocelli’s Con Te Partiro blasted out of the stadium’s speakers. Continue reading...

items.title: Mary Earps frustrates Arsenal as London City Lionesses earn battling draw
items.summary: Arsenal’s fifth draw from five home games in the Women’s Super League left them frustrated once again but this was a wholly different story to the previous four, as they played out an entertaining 1-1 draw with a London City Lionesses side inspired by their goalkeeper Mary Earps. Aston Villa, Birmingham, Manchester United and Crystal Palace all came to this stadium for a point, defending resolutely and exposing Arsenal’s inability to break down low blocks, whereas London City came to play and were rewarded with a draw that maintains their six‑point advantage over Arsenal in the race for a European place, and moving within six points of the leaders Chelsea. Continue reading...

items.title: Record-breaking Andy Robertson is Scotland’s finest captain
items.summary: As he passes Kenny Dalglish’s appearance total, it is important to remember that it is the left-back’s journey that sets him apart Andy Robertson may not be Scotland’s greatest player, but he is indisputably their finest captain. It counts as sacrilege, even to generations who have watched Kenny Dalglish only on YouTube, to reputationally place Robertson above the Liverpool hero on the basis of a cap haul that will reach 103 in St Gallen on Monday. Dalglish’s international career ended at 102 and the curious events that meant he missed the 1986 World Cup. There is no requirement to compare a left-back in 2026 to a forward from decades earlier. Dalglish and Robertson are men in different positions in essentially a different sport. Instead, Robertson’s march to the top of the cap pile gives cause to laud his contribution. Continue reading...

items.title: Wat zijn de gevolgen voor Rode Duivels van dolle Nations League-avond?

In de andere groep trok Engeland na een spectaculaire wedstrijd in Spanje aan het langste eind en pakte het eveneens de eerste plaats. items.title: Joga Bonito! Geweldige Rode Duivels swingend voorbij machteloos Italië

items.title: Terry Butcher: ‘I’ve learned to live with the Hand of God goal better’
items.summary: The former England centre-back answers your questions on Diego Maradona, Bobby Robson and on staying in strange places “Have you made up all these on your own?” asks Terry Butcher, sitting in a London office in the week he is presented with his England legacy cap. It turns out dozens of Guardian readers want to pick the brains of a much-loved centre-back who was feted en route to a World Cup semi-final and tormented four years previously by the mercurial genius of Diego Maradona. Did Maradona ever admit to the “Hand of God”? Butcher found himself in the post-match doping-control room alongside his nemesis at the Azteca in 1986. “I tapped my head, then my hand, and then he tapped his head,” Butcher says. “He didn’t admit to it because, if he had, I’d have been right across that room.” Continue reading...
